issues.description: The problem statement asks students to "Create a class BookRepository" (with an initializer init(books: [Book])), while the rest of the problem, the template, and the solution use the name `Bookstore`. This naming mismatch (BookRepository vs Bookstore) is structural: students following the problem text may implement `BookRepository` and then find that the template, tests, and example client expect a `Bookstore` type, causing compilation/test failures and confusion about which class to create.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the name consistent across artifacts. Either (a) change the problem statement to require a class named `Bookstore` (referring to init(books: [Book]) as described elsewhere), or (b) rename the class in the template and solution to `BookRepository` (and update all references such as assembleBookstore and tests). Preferably update the problem statement to use `Bookstore` so it matches the template and solution and avoids breaking existing tests.

issues.description: The problem statement asks for a class named `BookRepository` (including the init signature) but the template and the reference solution consistently use the name `Bookstore`. This naming mismatch for the same core entity (the class that holds the collection of books) creates mapping confusion: students will look for `BookRepository` per the instructions but the starter code, filenames, and tests expect `Bookstore`. This can cause students to implement the wrong identifier or be unable to connect the requirement to the provided template, leading to unnecessary confusion and failing tests.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the class name consistent across all artifacts. Prefer changing the problem statement to refer to `Bookstore` (to match file names, template, and solution). Replace the phrase `class BookRepository` with `class Bookstore` and keep the required initializer signature `init(books: [Book])`. Alternatively, if you intend the name `BookRepository`, update the template files and solution to use `BookRepository` everywhere, but keeping `Bookstore` is recommended for consistency with existing filenames and package naming.
